_comment: Char ceilings for the always-loaded canon and its companions. A ceiling is a MAX: shrinking always passes. Raising one needs --update in its own justified commit, with a reason. See scripts/check_claudemd_budget.py. CLAUDE.md is loaded into EVERY session, so its size is a standing tax on all work; it was 349,512 chars before the v1.130.0 canon/changelog split and is budgeted at 82,000 to leave real working room without letting the changelog creep back in. The archive is budgeted generously because it is a grep target that is never auto-loaded - it is listed only so that 'shrink CLAUDE.md' cannot be satisfied by moving weight somewhere nobody is watching. ARCHIVE CEILING RAISED 420,000 -> 430,000 (v1.145.14). Three consecutive commits (v1.145.10, v1.145.13, v1.146.0) each had to compress genuine post-mortem narrative to fit, and v1.145.13 evicted part of the entry it superseded and recorded that 'shaving is spent'. Compressing the record to satisfy a cap degrades the exact thing the cap exists to protect. The reason for capping the archive is displacement - so that 'shrink CLAUDE.md' cannot be satisfied by moving canon somewhere nobody watches - and that reason is unaffected here: the archive is a grep target, never auto-loaded, so its size is not a per-session tax. CLAUDE.md's own 82,000 is untouched and is the ceiling that actually matters. Raised by 10,000 (2.4%), not opened up, so the next raise is still a deliberate act. RAISED AGAIN AT v1.147.1, both files, for two DIFFERENT reasons - measured, not estimated. docs/Neural.md: origin/dev stood at 39,997 of 40,000 - THREE chars of headroom - and v1.147.0's pane-pager entry took it to 40,830 before the MC work touched it at all. A behaviour doc that is actively maintained cannot live on 3 chars; the next writer's only options were to compress someone else's paragraph or skip documenting their change, and the second is what actually happens. Raised to 43,000 (+7.5%). docs/Changelog-Archive.md: the v1.145.14 raise to 430,000 left 919 chars by the time v1.148.0's post-mortem was written - one entry of headroom, i.e. a ceiling-raise commit per entry, which turns a growth SIGNAL into a per-entry tax and pressures writers to under-document exactly the near-misses worth recording. Raised to 445,000 (+3.5%). Neither is opened up: both remain deliberate acts, and CLAUDE.md's 82,000 - the ceiling that is a per-session tax and the only one that truly matters - is untouched at 70,657. RAISED AGAIN AT v1.149.2, archive only, and this time the previous raise's own stated reason is the evidence. v1.147.1 raised the archive to 445,000 BECAUSE 919 chars of headroom is 'one entry of headroom, i.e. a ceiling-raise commit per entry'. Measured two versions later, at origin/dev c4f2226d6+2: 444,403 of 445,000, i.e. 597 spare - LESS headroom than the condition that triggered the raise, reached in two commits. A +2.4% and a +3.5% step have now each been consumed within three commits, so the step size, not the ceiling, is what is wrong: raised to 460,000 (+3.4%), which is ~3 entries at the observed ~5kB median rather than ~0.1. Still a deliberate act, still not opened up, and the displacement reason is still unaffected (the archive is a grep target, never auto-loaded, so its size is not a per-session tax). CLAUDE.md's own 82,000 - the only ceiling that IS a per-session tax - is untouched at 70,657. NOT RAISED, and flagged instead: docs/Neural.md stands at 42,913 of 43,000, i.e. 87 chars, which is the same trap v1.147.1 described for that file ('a behaviour doc that is actively maintained cannot live on 3 chars'). It is left alone here only because this commit does not touch it; the next writer who does will have to raise it first. RAISED AT v1.152.0, BOTH files, and for docs/Neural.md the previous note is the instruction: v1.149.2 measured it at 42,913 of 43,000 (87 chars) and wrote 'it is left alone here only because this commit does not touch it; the next writer who does will have to raise it first'. This is that commit — the concepts payload is a new thing the app fetches, so the payload table in the behaviour doc is exactly where it belongs, and origin/dev had already grown the file to 43,350 on its own. Raised 43,000 -> 45,000 (+4.7%), which is ~4 payload-table-sized edits rather than one. docs/Changelog-Archive.md: origin/dev stands at 458,507 of 460,000, i.e. 1,493 spare — under a third of one entry at the observed ~5kB median, and the v1.149.2 raise that set 460,000 was itself justified by 597 spare being too little. That raise targeted '~3 entries' and lasted three commits, so the step is still short: raised 460,000 -> 480,000 (+4.3%), leaving ~18,600 after this entry, i.e. 3-4 entries. Both remain deliberate acts. CLAUDE.md's own 82,000 — the only ceiling that is a per-session tax — is untouched and this commit does not add to it beyond one payload clause (70,813).
